From metabolic health to sustainable
fats: Where novel ingredients are poised
for the biggest exits
The novel ingredients sector is experiencing a
dramatic reset. After VC funding peaked at $5.3
billion in 2021, it dropped to $1.5 billion in 2024
—but investor interest persists, especially in
early-stage deals and high-growth segments like
precision fermentation, novel fats & oils, and
functional health-impact ingredients. This
analyst note breaks down where innovation and
capital are converging in the race to meet
growing demand for healthier, more sustainable,
and science-backed food ingredients.
Meanwhile, mature subsegments like first-gen
sweeteners, processed plant-based meats, and
novel salts are facing headwinds as consumers
shift toward “cleaner” and more functional
options.
We analyze the latest valuation trends, spotlight
promising startups, examine regional
investment shifts, and identify where the next
wave of exits will likely come from in this
evolving market. If you are tracking the future of
foodtech—from metabolic health to molecular
flavor—you will not want to miss this one.
